text.tspan: Microsoft Foundry hosted agents in a hub-and-spoke network
Prebuilt agent image in a private ACR · Azure Firewall with minimal rules · Private DNS Resolver as DNS server of every VNet
(public IP on the ACR allow list)
Azure Firewall policy: only these rules, everything else is denied
NETWORK TCP 443 agent subnet → AzureActiveDirectory service tag
NETWORK TCP 1688 VM subnet → Windows KMS (activation)
replies to vnet-ai go back through the firewall
custom DNS server of hub, dns and ai VNets
Private DNS zones (linked to vnet-dns only)
A records created by the private endpoint zone groups
answers from the linked private zones
RDP from the Azure portal to vm-test
The Developer SKU uses a shared pool,
VNet peering vnet-ai ↔ vnet-hub (forwarded traffic allowed).
Traffic to the private endpoints stays inside the VNet and does not go through the firewall.
Azure PaaS services (rg-ai), outside the VNet
Microsoft Foundry account · public network access Enabled
container image from the private ACR
Public access: only the allowed IPs, disabled when the list is empty
AcrPull for the Foundry project identity
Deploy: azd / Python SDK (Entra ID auth, HTTPS 443) → Foundry public endpoint →
new hosted agent version that points to the ACR image.
Image: az acr build / docker push → ACR public endpoint, only from the allowed IPs
(ACR Tasks runners need a temporary rule, no IP = no public access).
Test: Azure portal → Developer Bastion → RDP to vm-test (no public IP on the VM).
vm-test resolves the Foundry / ACR names to private IPs and calls the private
endpoints inside vnet-ai (system routes, not through the firewall).
Agent start: the platform pulls the image from ACR through the ACR private
The agent calls the Foundry project and the model through the Foundry private endpoint.
Private Link connection from each private endpoint to its PaaS service.
A client in snet-agent or snet-vm uses 10.1.0.4 as DNS server. vnet-dns is not
peered with vnet-ai, so the UDR sends the query to the firewall (rule: port 53).
The firewall forwards it over the hub ↔ dns peering to the Private DNS Resolver
inbound endpoint. The reply returns through the firewall (UDR rt-dns).
The resolver forwards the query to Azure-provided DNS 168.63.129.16 of vnet-dns.
Azure DNS answers from the private zones linked to vnet-dns: Foundry and ACR names
return the private endpoint IPs (10.2.0.x). Public names are resolved recursively.
All private zones live in rg-dns and are linked only to vnet-dns. The hub, dns and
ai VNets use the resolver as custom DNS server.
Agent subnet traffic leaves through the UDR next hop: the firewall.
The firewall only allows AzureActiveDirectory:443 and the identity / login FQDNs,
and SNATs through its public IP to Microsoft Entra ID (managed identity tokens).
Every other Internet destination is denied.
Foundry project identity: Foundry User on the account, AcrPull on the ACR
vm-test identity: Foundry User on the account, AcrPull on the ACR
Admin user (optional): Foundry User and Foundry Agent Consumer on the account;
AcrPush, AcrPull and Container Registry Tasks Contributor on the ACR
